item.title: Former Cocaine Addict Warns of Drug Epidemic in Rural Ireland
item.description: A former cocaine addict turned addiction counsellor says there's a drug epidemic in rural Ireland. Strokestown native Donal Hanly first started using cocaine in his late 20s. He says his addiction to the drug and to alcohol led to two suicide attempts. Advertisement The former Strokestown player won two county titles with the club before drugs took over his life. item.title: Shannonside Region to Enjoy Favourable Conditions Over Christmas
item.description: The Shannonside region will see favourable conditions during the Christmas period. While it won’t be a white Christmas, the sprinkling of frost on Christmas morning will be sure to add some excitement. And as for those post-dinner walks on Christmas Day, they will be possible, as frost will clear to leave a dry, bright day with plenty of sunshine for most. item.title: Parcels Delivered in North Roscommon Double Over Three Christmases
item.description: The number of parcels delivered in north Roscommon has doubled over the past three Christmases. But there has been a big drop in Christmas cards. An Post will continue to collect and deliver post today and tomorrow. Advertisement Sean Moylan is the manager of the sorting office in Boyle - he says it's been a mixed picture this Christmas:

item.title: No Injuries Reported in North Roscommon Crash
item.description: No injuries have been reported following an early morning crash in north Roscommon. Gardaí and emergency services attended the two-vehicle collision between Keadue and Leitrim Village at Battlebridge. The incident occurred shortly after 12.30am. Advertisement Gardaí say it has now been cleared and traffic is moving freely again.

item.title: 20 Patients Waiting for Beds at Local Hospital This Morning
item.description: There were 20 patients waiting for beds at a local hospital this morning. That's according to the Irish Nurses and Midwives Organisation figures, which show over 176 patients were waiting for a bed at facilities nationwide. Sligo University Hospital is the busiest in the region and second busiest in the country today with 20 people waiting for bed. item.title: Decision delayed on controversial Roscommon wind farm
item.description: A decision on the planning application for a controversial wind farm in Roscommon has been delayed. Ballyfeeney Green Energy applied for permission to build six turbines between Scramogue and Kilglass. Over 150 people objected and a decision was due today. Advertisement But Roscommon County Council has sought more information from the developers - which has stalled the planning process. item.title: Almost 900 Ukrainians living in Roscommon homes this Christmas - as Bishop expresses 'solidarity' with refugees
item.description: Almost 900 Ukrainian refugees are living in people's homes in Co Roscommon this Christmas. They're staying in 280 houses around the county. The property owners are getting €600 a week, under the government's Offer a Home Programme. item.title: 24 New Speed Camera Zones to Go Live Across Shannonside from January 1st
item.description: Gardaí are cracking down on speeders in the Shannonside region with 24 new speed camera zones becoming operational from 1st January. The primary purpose of safety cameras is to reduce speed-related collisions, lessen injuries and save lives on Irish roads. Longford will have three with one more community request, while Leitrim will have a further six safety camera zones.
